d.d: An implement for washing floors or similar, made of a piece of cloth, or a collection of thrums, or coarse yarn, fastened to a handle.
A wash with a mop; the act of mopping.
d.x: He gave the floor a quick mop to soak up the spilt juice.

d.d: An annual fair where servants were historically hired.
To rub, scrub, clean or wipe with a mop, or as if with a mop.
To make a wry expression with the mouth.
To carry oneself in a depressed, lackadaisical manner; to give oneself up to low spirits; to pout, sulk.
To make spiritless and stupid.
The act of moping
d.x: When she gets upset, she has a little mope, and then gets over it.

d.d: A lightweight, two-wheeled vehicle equipped with a small motor and pedals, designed to go no faster than some specified speed limit.
d.x: He took his moped into work.
